strings.d1.s0.name: Koutoubia Mosque
strings.d1.s0.tips: A 77 m minaret (twin of the Giralda in Seville). See it from outside and walk the gardens; it works as the medina's compass.
strings.d1.s1.name: Bahia Palace
strings.d1.s1.tips: A 19th-century vizier's palace with cedar ceilings and courtyards. It is quiet in the first hour.
strings.d1.s2.name: Saadian Tombs
strings.d1.s2.tips: 16th-century mausoleums rediscovered in 1917, with Carrara marble.
strings.d1.s3.name: Souks Marrakech
strings.d1.s3.tips: Labyrinthine markets selling leather (the Bab Debbagh tannery), lamps and carpets. Offer a third of the first price and turn down guide offers.
strings.d1.s4.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa at Night
strings.d1.s4.tips: A UNESCO-listed square with 100+ food stalls (harira, merguez, snails), storytellers and the Café de France terrace. Snake charmers will ask for money.
strings.d1.b0.name: Le Jardin Secret
strings.d1.b0.tips: A restored riad garden and tower: shade instead of the souks.
strings.d1.b1.name: Nomad Marrakech
strings.d1.b1.tips: Modern Moroccan food on a rooftop in Rahba Kedima. Book ahead.
strings.d2.s0.name: Jardin Majorelle
strings.d2.s0.tips: A cobalt-blue villa and cactus garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Buy tickets online for the 08:00 opening (they sell out); the Berber Museum is included.
strings.d2.s1.name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent
strings.d2.s1.tips: The museum next door. Combined ticket available, with a cafeteria.
strings.d2.s2.name: Gueliz Avenue Mohammed V
strings.d2.s2.tips: The French new town, with galleries and the 33 Rue Majorelle concept store.
strings.d2.s3.name: Grand Café de la Poste
strings.d2.s4.name: Menara Gardens
strings.d2.s4.tips: A 12th-century pool and pavilion. In winter you get views of the snowy Atlas peaks; come at sunset.
strings.d2.b0.name: Amal Women's Training Center
strings.d2.b0.tips: A restaurant run by a women's cooperative. Couscous on Fridays.
strings.d2.b1.name: Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam
strings.d2.b1.tips: A shaded park beside the medina, a closer alternative to Menara.
strings.d3.s0.name: Imlil Village
strings.d3.s0.tips: 1.5 hours by taxi or tour (1,740 m). A Berber village at the foot of Toubkal, with mules and walnut trees.
strings.d3.s1.name: Aroumd Village Walk
strings.d3.s1.tips: A 1-hour climb from Imlil (guide 200 MAD). Terraced gardens and views of Toubkal, with snow in winter.
strings.d3.s2.name: Berber Home Lunch
strings.d3.s2.tips: Tagine and mint tea in a family home, on a terrace.
strings.d3.s3.name: Kasbah du Toubkal Terrace
strings.d3.s3.tips: Tea at a mountain kasbah with valley views. Proceeds support charity.
strings.d3.s4.name: Imlil Waterfall
strings.d3.s4.tips: A short walk above the village. Head back by 17:00.
strings.d3.b0.name: Ourika Valley Setti Fatma
strings.d3.b0.tips: An alternative valley: a 7-waterfall hike and riverside tagine. More touristy.
strings.d3.b1.name: Café Aksaoual Imlil
strings.d3.b1.tips: A café on the village square.
strings.d4.s0.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
strings.d4.s0.tips: A 14th-century madrasa with zellij tilework and a cedar courtyard, 130 student cells, restored.
strings.d4.s1.name: Maison de la Photographie
strings.d4.s1.tips: Photographs of Morocco from 1870–1950. Coffee on the roof terrace with medina views.
strings.d4.s2.name: Le Jardin Marrakech
strings.d4.s2.tips: A restaurant in a green courtyard with tortoises, in Sidi Abdelaziz.
strings.d4.s3.name: Hammam de la Rose
strings.d4.s3.tips: A traditional hammam with black soap scrub mitt and argan massage. Separate hours for men and women.
strings.d4.s4.name: Terrasse des Épices
strings.d4.s4.tips: A rooftop restaurant with sunset views over the medina and tagine.
strings.d4.b0.name: Hammam Mouassine
strings.d4.b0.tips: A local public hammam: cheap, bring your own scrub mitt.
strings.d4.b1.name: Dar Cherifa
strings.d4.b1.tips: A 16th-century riad café-gallery with a literary focus.
strings.d5.s0.name: Skala de la Kasbah
strings.d5.s0.tips: 3 hours by Supratours bus (leaves Marrakech 07:00). Atlantic ramparts and cannons, a Game of Thrones filming location, and gulls.
strings.d5.s1.name: Essaouira Medina
strings.d5.s1.tips: A white-and-blue UNESCO medina with thuya wood workshops and art galleries.
strings.d5.s2.name: Essaouira Fishing Port
strings.d5.s2.tips: Fresh fish from the blue boats in the harbour, grilled at the stalls. Haggle by the kilo; try the sardines.
strings.d5.s3.name: Essaouira Beach
strings.d5.s3.tips: Winter wind and waves. Good for a walk along the shore.
strings.d5.s4.name: Taros Café
strings.d5.s4.tips: A rooftop terrace overlooking the harbour with gnawa music. Take the 17:30 bus back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Sidi Kaouki
strings.d5.b0.tips: A surf village beach 25 km away. Go by taxi.
strings.d5.b1.name: La Table by Madada
strings.d6.s0.name: Mellah and Lazama Synagogue
strings.d6.s0.tips: The old Jewish quarter, with a spice market, the synagogue and the Miâara cemetery.
strings.d6.s1.name: Dar Si Said Museum
strings.d6.s1.tips: A museum of Moroccan carpets and woodwork, with the most beautiful courtyard.
strings.d6.s2.name: Marché Central Gueliz
strings.d6.s2.tips: The new town market: fruit and a quick lunch.
strings.d6.s3.name: Agafay Desert
strings.d6.s3.tips: A stony desert 40 minutes from the city. Camel rides, quad biking, sunset tea and camp dinner (tour about 400 MAD).
strings.d6.s4.name: Agafay Desert Camp Dinner
strings.d6.s4.tips: Tagine and Berber music at the camp, included in the tour. Stargazing.
strings.d6.b0.name: Palmeraie Camel Ride
strings.d6.b0.tips: A palm grove next to the city, a closer alternative to Agafay.
strings.d6.b1.name: Al Fassia Gueliz
strings.d6.b1.tips: Women-run Moroccan classics, including lamb shank.
strings.d7.theme: El Badi and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: El Badi Palace
strings.d7.s0.tips: The ruins of a 16th-century 'incomparable' palace, with storks and pools, and the Koutoubia minbar.
strings.d7.s1.name: Place des Ferblantiers
strings.d7.s1.tips: The tinsmiths' square. Buy lamps as souvenirs and have a drink on the Kosybar terrace.
strings.d7.s2.name: Bacha Coffee Dar el Bacha
strings.d7.s2.tips: A coffee salon in a 1910 pasha's palace with 200 coffees. Expect a queue; a fitting farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Marrakech Menara Airport
strings.d7.b0.name: Dar el Bacha Museum
strings.d7.b0.tips: A museum of cultural confluence, instead of the coffee.
strings.d7.b1.name: Patisserie des Princes
strings.d7.b1.tips: Moroccan sweets (kaab el ghzal), near Bab Agnaou.
strings.note0: Petit taxis are metered (insist on it; 20–30 MAD), and the Careem app works. The medina is walkable. The airport taxi is a fixed 150 MAD; bus 19 costs 30 MAD.
strings.note1: October to April is ideal (20–25°C). Winter nights drop to 5°C and the Atlas is snowy (snow in Imlil). December and January are crowded; March and April bring orange blossom.
strings.note2: Stay in a riad (courtyard house) inside the medina; a porter for your luggage costs 20 MAD. The bargaining rule is a third of the first price. Offers of a 'guide' and the 'this road is closed' trick are scams.
strings.note3: Tagine 60–100 MAD, Jemaa stall meal 50, mint tea 15, Majorelle 170 (online), hammam 100–400; tip 10 MAD.
strings.note4: Women will be more comfortable with shoulders and knees covered. Mosque interiors are closed to non-Muslims (Koutoubia is seen from outside).
strings.note5: Turkish citizens can stay 90 days without a visa. Carry cash in MAD (from ATMs); cards work at riads and restaurants.
